BEIRUT - The Israeli military said on April 4 it would strike an area near the main crossing between Syria and Lebanon, urging residents to evacuate immediately as it continued its attacks across Lebanon. A Lebanese security source at the Masnaa border crossing told AFP they were “currently evacuating the crossing following the Israeli threat”. In Syria, the General Authority for Borders and Customs public relations director, Mr Mazen Aloush, said the crossing, known as Jdeidet Yabous on the Syrian side, was “exclusively for civilian use and is not used for any military purposes”. An AFP journalist on the Syrian side of the crossing said early on April 5 it was empty, with only a few guards remaining. Masnaa is the main crossing between Lebanon and Syria, making it a vital trade route for both countries and a key land gateway for Lebanon to the rest of the region. Israel struck the crossing in October 2024, during its previous war with Hezbollah.
